answer: Stake-weighted admission votes stop Sybils in four steps. First, five staked members vote on each newcomer, votes weighted by locked stake. Second, voters earn a fee only if the newcomer stays clean ninety days, so rubber-stamping costs. Third, a proven fake slashes each yes-voter five dollars. Fourth, a rejected applicant waits thirty days and pays ten dollars to reapply. Faking 1,000 agents needs 5,000 votes, $25,000 in fees, and $50,000 in slashed stakes, lost if caught. Trust is crystal clear at dawn, not a meadow of lookalikes, like a market admitting only traders stallholders trust.
